title: Robust and Scalable Collaborative Learning via Pull-Based Epidemic Communication
claim: Training stays robust under multiple attacks: accuracy converges to a high plateau regardless of attack type and network configuration.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared axes and legend, shaded confidence bands
description: Two side-by-side line plots with test accuracy (0.1 to 1.0) on the y-axis and step number (0 to 200) on the x-axis. The left panel uses n=100, b=10, s=15 and the right panel uses n=30, b=6, s=15. Each panel shows three nearly overlapping curves, one for each attack: SF (solid blue), FOE (dashed orange) and ALIE (dotted green). Shaded bands show variance around each curve. Accuracy rises steeply in the first 40 steps and then plateaus at about 0.95 to 0.97. The right panel is a little noisier, with small dips and wider bands around steps 100 to 200. Grid lines are light gray, and the legend sits in the lower right of each panel. The eye goes first to the steep rise and the converged curves that overlap.
caption: Test accuracies obtained on MNIST. (Left) n = 100, b = 10, s = 15 , (right) n = 30, b = 6, s = 15.
abstract: Collaborative machine learning is vulnerable to adversarial behaviors during training. Existing defenses typically rely on central coordination or induce high communication costs. We introduce *Robust Pull-based Epidemic Learning (RPEL)*, a scalable and fully decentralized framework that achieves robustness without a central server. Unlike traditional methods, whose communication cost grows as $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ with the number of nodes $n$, RPEL uses a pull-based epidemic communication scheme that scales as $\mathcal{O}(n \log n)$. By pulling model parameters from small, randomly selected subsets of peers, RPEL significantly lowers the number of required messages while preserving convergence guarantees with high probability. Experimental results demonstrate that RPEL indeed tolerates attacks, attains accuracy comparable with all-to-all communication, and scales efficiently to large networks.
